title: WebSockets
subtitle: Persistent bi-directional TCP communication vs short polling, long polling, and Server-Sent Events (SSE).
keyTakeaways: WebSockets upgrade an initial HTTP connection into a persistent, full-duplex TCP socket, allowing either client or server to send frames with minimal framing overhead.
For unidirectional server-to-client updates (like stock tickers or notification feeds), Server-Sent Events (SSE) over HTTP/2 is often simpler and avoids WebSocket operational headaches.
Operating stateful WebSocket clusters requires a pub/sub backplane (Redis Pub/Sub or Kafka) so an update landed on Server A can reach a client connected to Server B.
architectureDiagram:
REAL-TIME SPECTRUM & WEBSOCKET PUB/SUB BACKPLANE
[ Client 1 ] ==== Persistent WS ====> [ WS Gateway Node A ]
                                              |
                                     [ Redis Pub/Sub Backplane ]
                                              |
[ Client 2 ] <=== Persistent WS ====== [ WS Gateway Node B ]
(Client 1 sends message -> Node A publishes to Redis -> Node B delivers to Client 2)

sections.heading: The Real-Time Communication Spectrum
sections.body: Choosing a real-time protocol depends on directionality, connection volume, and payload frequency. Naive HTTP short polling wastes bandwidth sending empty requests every few seconds. HTTP long polling holds connections open until data arrives, but requires tearing down and renegotiating TCP connections on every message. WebSockets solve this by executing an HTTP `101 Switching Protocols` handshake and reusing the underlying TCP socket for arbitrary bi-directional framing with barely 2 bytes of header overhead.
bullets: Short Polling: Periodic client HTTP requests; heavy network header waste and high database load on idle systems.
Long Polling (Comet): Client holds request open until server responds; better latency than short polling, but requires frequent connection recreation.
Server-Sent Events (SSE): Unidirectional, text-based streaming from server to client over standard HTTP; automatic reconnection and HTTP/2 multiplexing out of the box.
WebSockets: Full-duplex, bi-directional, binary-capable persistent TCP connection; ideal for low-latency bidirectional interaction.

sections.heading: Production Realities of Stateful WebSocket Fleets
sections.body: Unlike stateless REST APIs where requests route randomly across any server, WebSocket connections are long-lived and pinned to a specific physical node. This architectural shift introduces unique operational challenges during scaling, deployments, and cluster failover.
bullets: Pub/Sub Distribution Layer: Because two users in a chat room will connect to different WebSocket gateway instances, nodes must communicate via a shared backplane (Redis Pub/Sub, Kafka, or RabbitMQ) to deliver messages across nodes.

Thundering Herd on Deployment: Rolling out a new software release terminates millions of active sockets simultaneously; clients must use exponential backoff with randomized jitter to prevent crushing the edge during reconnects.

Connection Limits and Memory: A single Linux box can support 500,000+ idle WebSockets with tuned `net.ipv4` kernel settings, but allocating 10KB of memory per socket means 1M connections consume ~10 GB RAM purely for TCP buffer overhead.

tradeOffs.pros: True full-duplex bi-directional communication; ultra-low framing overhead (2-10 bytes per frame); sub-10ms delivery latency.
tradeOffs.cons: Stateful servers complicate rolling deployments; requires cross-node pub/sub backplane; proxy/load-balancer timeouts need heartbeat pings.
tradeOffs.bestFor: Real-time chat apps, collaborative whiteboards (Figma), multiplayer gaming, and high-frequency trading terminal feeds.

tradeOffs.pros: Native HTTP/2 support; automatic browser reconnection logic; works seamlessly through standard corporate proxies and firewalls.
tradeOffs.cons: Unidirectional only (server to client); client-to-server messages must use separate HTTP POST requests.
tradeOffs.bestFor: Live financial stock tickers, push notification feeds, system monitoring dashboards, and LLM text generation streaming.

interviewTip: When designing a real-time notification or chat system, evaluate whether you actually need bi-directional communication. If the client only receives updates and sends messages via standard REST POST requests, recommending Server-Sent Events (SSE) over HTTP/2 demonstrates practical restraint.
